# hq-review

Review in your own worktree or workspace, never in the author's. Prefer a reviewer from a
different vendor than the author (the PR's `agent:*` label).

1. Check out the PR: `gh pr checkout <PR>`.
2. Find the issue: `gh pr view <PR> --json title,labels,closingIssuesReferences`, then
   `gh issue view <N>`. Note the Acceptance criteria, Scope and Do not touch.
3. Read the diff: `gh pr diff <PR>`. Flag any file outside Scope or inside Do not touch.
4. Run `./hq check` and the issue's Verify steps.
5. If `command -v claude && command -v codex` succeeds, run `entire review`. It runs Claude Code
   and Codex reviewers plus a judge from the shared profile and posts to the trail. Otherwise
   review by hand against each acceptance criterion.
6. Write the verdict to `.context/review-<PR>.md`:
   - Verdict: pass or changes.
   - Each acceptance criterion: met or not met, with evidence.
   - Findings, blocking first: `file:line`, the problem, a suggested fix.
   - The tail of `./hq check`.
7. Post it: `gh pr review <PR> --comment --body-file .context/review-<PR>.md`.
   Use `--comment`: you cannot approve a PR opened from your own account.
8. Label it:
   - pass: `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass --remove-label review:changes`
   - changes: `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:changes --remove-label review:pass`
9. Do not push fixes to the author's branch and do not merge. Tell the human the verdict.

+import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
+import { roadTrafficDisturbance } from "../domain";
+import sensorsFixture from "./fixtures/city-sensors.json";
+import { citySensors, sensorLevel } from "./sensors";
+
+describe("city sensor fixture", () => {
+  const sensors = citySensors.parse(sensorsFixture);
+
+  test("holds about ten Newcastle sensors, all indicative", () => {
+    expect(sensors).toHaveLength(10);
+    expect(sensors.every((s) => s.indicative)).toBe(true);
+    expect(new Set(sensors.map((s) => s.id)).size).toBe(sensors.length);
+  });
+
+  test("covers shaded, out-of-range and not-enough-data sensors", () => {
+    expect(sensors.some((s) => !s.notEnoughData && !s.outOfRange)).toBe(true);
+    expect(sensors.some((s) => s.outOfRange)).toBe(true);
+    expect(sensors.some((s) => s.notEnoughData)).toBe(true);
+  });
+
+  test("%HSD follows the WHO curve", () => {
+    for (const s of sensors) {
+      if (s.lnight30 === null) continue;
+      const expected = roadTrafficDisturbance(s.lnight30);
+      expect(s.pctHighlySleepDisturbed).toBeCloseTo(expected.percentHighlyDisturbed, 1);
+      expect(s.outOfRange).toBe(expected.outOfRange);
+    }
+  });
+
+  test("not enough data means fewer than 30 nights", () => {
+    for (const s of sensors) expect(s.notEnoughData).toBe(s.nights < 30);
+  });
+
+  test("rejects a non-indicative sensor and a missing estimate", () => {
+    expect(sensorLevel.safeParse({ ...sensors[0], indicative: false }).success).toBe(false);
+    expect(sensorLevel.safeParse({ ...sensors[0], lnight30: null }).success).toBe(false);
+  });
+});

@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
+import { z } from "zod";
+
+/**
+ * One Newcastle Urban Observatory noise sensor on the city map.
+ * Figures are an indicative road-traffic estimate, never a measured disturbance rate
+ * (`docs/DOMAIN.md`).
+ */
+export const sensorLevel = z
+  .object({
+    id: z.string().min(1),
+    name: z.string().min(1),
+    lat: z.number().min(-90).max(90),
+    lon: z.number().min(-180).max(180),
+    /** Energy average of nightly Lnight in dB; null when there is not enough data */
+    lnight30: z.number().nullable(),
+    /** Nights of data behind the estimate */
+    nights: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
+    /** Indicative % highly sleep disturbed from the WHO curve; null when there is not enough data */
+    pctHighlySleepDisturbed: z.number().nullable(),
+    /** Lnight fell outside 40 to 65 dB and was clamped for the estimate */
+    outOfRange: z.boolean(),
+    /** Fewer than 30 nights: show the sensor but don't shade it */
+    notEnoughData: z.boolean(),
+    indicative: z.literal(true),
+    /** ISO 8601 timestamp of the latest reading used */
+    updatedAt: z.iso.datetime(),
+  })
+  .refine((s) => !s.notEnoughData || (s.lnight30 === null && s.pctHighlySleepDisturbed === null), {
+    message: "a sensor without enough data has no Lnight or %HSD",
+  })
+  .refine((s) => s.notEnoughData || (s.lnight30 !== null && s.pctHighlySleepDisturbed !== null), {
+    message: "a sensor with enough data needs Lnight and %HSD",
+  });
+export type SensorLevel = z.infer<typeof sensorLevel>;
+
+/** Output of the city sensors query. */
+export const citySensors = z.array(sensorLevel);
+export type CitySensors = z.infer<typeof citySensors>;
